units.leftText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
units.rightText: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

units.leftText: The same was in the beginning with God.
units.rightText: The same was in the beginning with God.

units.leftText: All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.
units.rightText: All things were made through him; and without him was not anything made that hath been made.

units.leftText: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
units.rightText: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.

units.leftText: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
units.rightText: And the light shineth in the darkness; and the darkness apprehended it not.
leftNotes: 1:5 The word translated “overcome” (κατέλαβεν) can also be translated “comprehended.” It refers to getting a grip on an enemy to defeat him.

units.leftText: There came a man sent from God, whose name was John.
units.rightText: There came a man, sent from God, whose name was John.

units.leftText: The same came as a witness, that he might testify about the light, that all might believe through him.
units.rightText: The same came for witness, that he might bear witness of the light, that all might believe through him.

units.leftText: He was not the light, but was sent that he might testify about the light.
units.rightText: He was not the light, but came that he might bear witness of the light.

units.leftText: The true light that enlightens everyone was coming into the world.
units.rightText: There was the true light, even the light which lighteth every man, coming into the world.

units.leftText: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world didn’t recognize him.
units.rightText: He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world knew him not.

units.leftText: He came to his own, and those who were his own didn’t receive him.
units.rightText: He came unto his own, and they that were his own received him not.

units.leftText: But as many as received him, to them he gave the right to become God’s children, to those who believe in his name:
units.rightText: But as many as received him, to them gave he the right to become children of God, even to them that believe on his name:

units.leftText: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
units.rightText: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

units.leftText: The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
units.rightText: And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us (and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten from the Father), full of grace and truth.
leftNotes: 1:14 The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενους”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.

units.leftText: John testified about him. He cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me has surpassed me, for he was before me.’”
units.rightText: John beareth witness of him, and crieth, saying, This was he of whom I said, He that cometh after me is become before me: for he was before me.

units.leftText: From his fullness we all received grace upon grace.
units.rightText: For of his fulness we all received, and grace for grace.

units.leftText: For the law was given through Moses. Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: No one has seen God at any time. The only born Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.
units.rightText: No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.
leftNotes: 1:18 The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενη”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.

units.leftText: This is John’s testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
units.rightText: And this is the witness of John, when the Jews sent unto him from Jerusalem priests and Levites to ask him, Who art thou?

units.leftText: He declared, and didn’t deny, but he declared, “I am not the Christ.”
units.rightText: And he confessed, and denied not; and he confessed, I am not the Christ.

units.leftText: They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?”
units.rightText: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elijah? And he saith, I am not. Art thou the prophet? And he answered, No.

units.leftText: They said therefore to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?

units.leftText: He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet said.”
units.rightText: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said Isaiah the prophet.

units.leftText: The ones who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
units.rightText: And they had been sent from the Pharisees.

units.leftText: They asked him, “Why then do you baptize if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”
units.rightText: And they asked him, and said unto him, Why then baptizest thou, if thou art not the Christ, neither Elijah, neither the prophet?

units.leftText: John answered them, “I baptize in water, but among you stands one whom you don’t know.
units.rightText: John answered them, saying, I baptize in water: in the midst of you standeth one whom ye know not,

units.leftText: He is the one who comes after me, who is preferred before me, whose sandal strap I’m not worthy to loosen.”
units.rightText: even he that cometh after me, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to unloose.

units.leftText: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
units.rightText: These things were done in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

units.leftText: The next day, he saw Jesus coming to him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
units.rightText: On the morrow he seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God, that taketh away the sin of the world!
leftNotes: 1:29 “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: This is he of whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who is preferred before me, for he was before me.’
units.rightText: This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man who is become before me: for he was before me.

units.leftText: I didn’t know him, but for this reason I came baptizing in water, that he would be revealed to Israel.”
units.rightText: And I knew him not; but that he should be made manifest to Israel, for this cause came I baptizing in water.

units.leftText: John testified, saying, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him.
units.rightText: And John bare witness, saying, I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove out of heaven; and it abode upon him.

units.leftText: I didn’t recognize him, but he who sent me to baptize in water said to me, ‘On whomever you will see the Spirit descending and remaining on him is he who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’
units.rightText: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize in water, he said unto me, Upon whomsoever thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and abiding upon him, the same is he that baptizeth in the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.”
units.rightText: And I have seen, and have borne witness that this is the Son of God.

units.leftText: Again, the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples,
units.rightText: Again on the morrow John was standing, and two of his disciples;

units.leftText: and he looked at Jesus as he walked, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!”
units.rightText: and he looked upon Jesus as he walked, and saith, Behold, the Lamb of God!

units.leftText: The two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
units.rightText: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.

units.leftText: Jesus turned and saw them following, and said to them, “What are you looking for?”
units.rightText: And Jesus turned, and beheld them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? And they said unto him, Rabbi (which is to say, being interpreted, Teacher), where abidest thou?

units.leftText: He said to them, “Come and see.”
units.rightText: He saith unto them, Come, and ye shall see. They came therefore and saw where he abode; and they abode with him that day: it was about the tenth hour.

units.leftText: One of the two who heard John and followed him was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
units.rightText: One of the two that heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

units.leftText: He first found his own brother, Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah!” (which is, being interpreted, Christ ).
units.rightText: He findeth first his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messiah (which is, being interpreted, Christ).

units.leftText: He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas” (which is by interpretation, Peter).
units.rightText: He brought him unto Jesus. Jesus looked upon him, and said, Thou art Simon the son of John: thou shalt be called Cephas (which is by interpretation, Peter).

units.leftText: On the next day, he was determined to go out into Galilee, and he found Philip. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.”
units.rightText: On the morrow he was minded to go forth into Galilee, and he findeth Philip: and Jesus saith unto him, Follow me.

units.leftText: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
units.rightText: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.

units.leftText: Philip found Nathanael, and said to him, “We have found him of whom Moses in the law and also the prophets, wrote: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”
units.rightText: Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, wrote, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.

units.leftText: Nathanael said to him, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?”
units.rightText: And Nathanael said unto him, Can any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.

units.leftText: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and said about him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!”
units.rightText: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!

units.leftText: Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?”
units.rightText: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.

units.leftText: Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are King of Israel!”
units.rightText: Nathanael answered him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art King of Israel.

units.leftText: Jesus answered him, “Because I told you, ‘I saw you underneath the fig tree,’ do you believe? You will see greater things than these!”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee underneath the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these.

units.leftText: He said to him, “Most certainly, I tell you all, hereafter you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye shall see the heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.

units.leftText: The third day, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there.
units.rightText: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:

units.leftText: Jesus also was invited, with his disciples, to the wedding.
units.rightText: and Jesus also was bidden, and his disciples, to the marriage.

units.leftText: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.”
units.rightText: And when the wine failed, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.

units.leftText: Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does that have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.”
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.

units.leftText: His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.”
units.rightText: His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.

units.leftText: Now there were six water pots of stone set there after the Jews’ way of purifying, containing two or three metretes apiece.
units.rightText: Now there were six waterpots of stone set there after the Jews’ manner of purifying, containing two or three firkins apiece.
leftNotes: 2:6 2 to 3 metretes is about 20 to 30 U. S. Gallons, or 75 to 115 liters.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Fill the water pots with water.” So they filled them up to the brim.
units.rightText: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Now draw some out, and take it to the ruler of the feast.” So they took it.
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the ruler of the feast. And they bare it.

units.leftText: When the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and didn’t know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast called the bridegroom
units.rightText: And when the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and knew not whence it was (but the servants that had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast calleth the bridegroom,

units.leftText: and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk freely, then that which is worse. You have kept the good wine until now!”
units.rightText: and saith unto him, Every man setteth on first the good wine; and when men have drunk freely, then that which is worse: thou hast kept the good wine until now.

units.leftText: This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.
units.rightText: This beginning of his signs did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

units.leftText: After this, he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; and they stayed there a few days.
units.rightText: After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples; and there they abode not many days.

units.leftText: The Passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And the passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: He found in the temple those who sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting.
units.rightText: And he found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:

units.leftText: He made a whip of cords and drove all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money and overthrew their tables.
units.rightText: and he made a scourge of cords, and cast all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew their tables;

units.leftText: To those who sold the doves, he said, “Take these things out of here! Don’t make my Father’s house a marketplace!”
units.rightText: and to them that sold the doves he said, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house a house of merchandise.

units.leftText: His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will eat me up.”
units.rightText: His disciples remembered that it was written, Zeal for thy house shall eat me up.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore answered him, “What sign do you show us, seeing that you do these things?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore answered and said unto him, What sign showest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore said, “It took forty-six years to build this temple! Will you raise it up in three days?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou raise it up in three days?

units.leftText: But he spoke of the temple of his body.
units.rightText: But he spake of the temple of his body.

units.leftText: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus had said.
units.rightText: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he spake this; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.

units.leftText: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in his name, observing his signs which he did.
units.rightText: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, during the feast, many believed on his name, beholding his signs which he did.

units.leftText: But Jesus didn’t entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone,
units.rightText: But Jesus did not trust himself unto them, for that he knew all men,

units.leftText: and because he didn’t need for anyone to testify concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man.
units.rightText: and because he needed not that any one should bear witness concerning man; for he himself knew what was in man.

units.leftText: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
units.rightText: Now there was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews:

units.leftText: He came to Jesus by night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him.”
units.rightText: the same came unto him by night, and said to him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God; for no one can do these signs that thou doest, except God be with him.

units.leftText: Jesus answered him, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
leftNotes: 3:3 The word translated “anew” here and in John 3:7 (ἄνωθεν) also means “again” and “from above”.

units.leftText: Nicodemus said to him, “How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born?”
units.rightText: Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter a second time into his mother’s womb, and be born?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Most certainly I tell you, unless one is born of water and Spirit, he can’t enter into God’s Kingdom.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except one be born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: That which is born of the flesh is flesh. That which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
units.rightText: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.

units.leftText: Don’t marvel that I said to you, ‘You must all be born anew.’
units.rightText: Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born anew.

units.leftText: The wind blows where it wants to, and you hear its sound, but don’t know where it comes from and where it is going. So is everyone who is born of the Spirit.”
units.rightText: The wind bloweth where it will, and thou hearest the voice thereof, but knowest not whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
leftNotes: 3:8 The same Greek word (πνεῦμα) means wind, breath, and spirit.

units.leftText: Nicodemus answered him, “How can these things be?”
units.rightText: Nicodemus answered and said unto him, How can these things be?

units.leftText: Jesus answered him, “Are you the teacher of Israel, and don’t understand these things?
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto him, Art thou the teacher of Israel, and understandest not these things?

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, we speak that which we know and testify of that which we have seen, and you don’t receive our witness.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that which we know, and bear witness of that which we have seen; and ye receive not our witness.

units.leftText: If I told you earthly things and you don’t believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
units.rightText: If I told you earthly things and ye believe not, how shall ye believe if I tell you heavenly things?

units.leftText: No one has ascended into heaven but he who descended out of heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
units.rightText: And no one hath ascended into heaven, but he that descended out of heaven, even the Son of man, who is in heaven.

units.leftText: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
units.rightText: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up;

units.leftText: that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
units.rightText: that whosoever believeth may in him have eternal life.

units.leftText: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
units.rightText: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth on him should not perish, but have eternal life.
leftNotes: 3:16 The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενη”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.

units.leftText: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.
units.rightText: For God sent not the Son into the world to judge the world; but that the world should be saved through him.

units.leftText: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God.
units.rightText: He that believeth on him is not judged: he that believeth not hath been judged already, because he hath not believed on the name of the only begotten Son of God.

units.leftText: This is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were evil.
units.rightText: And this is the judgment, that the light is come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light; for their works were evil.

units.leftText: For everyone who does evil hates the light and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.
units.rightText: For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, and cometh not to the light, lest his works should be reproved.

units.leftText: But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.”
units.rightText: But he that doeth the truth cometh to the light, that his works may be made manifest, that they have been wrought in God.

units.leftText: After these things, Jesus came with his disciples into the land of Judea. He stayed there with them and baptized.
units.rightText: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judæa; and there he tarried with them, and baptized.

units.leftText: John also was baptizing in Enon near Salim, because there was much water there. They came and were baptized;
units.rightText: And John also was baptizing in Ænon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.

units.leftText: for John was not yet thrown into prison.
units.rightText: For John was not yet cast into prison.

units.leftText: Therefore a dispute arose on the part of John’s disciples with some Jews about purification.
units.rightText: There arose therefore a questioning on the part of John’s disciples with a Jew about purifying.

units.leftText: They came to John and said to him, “Rabbi, he who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified, behold, he baptizes, and everyone is coming to him.”
units.rightText: And they came unto John, and said to him, Rabbi, he that was with thee beyond the Jordan, to whom thou hast borne witness, behold, the same baptizeth, and all men come to him.

units.leftText: John answered, “A man can receive nothing unless it has been given him from heaven.
units.rightText: John answered and said, A man can receive nothing, except it have been given him from heaven.

units.leftText: You yourselves testify that I said, ‘I am not the Christ,’ but, ‘I have been sent before him.’
units.rightText: Ye yourselves bear me witness, that I said, I am not the Christ, but, that I am sent before him.

units.leftText: He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice. Therefore my joy is made full.
units.rightText: He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, that standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice: this my joy therefore is made full.

units.leftText: He must increase, but I must decrease.
units.rightText: He must increase, but I must decrease.

units.leftText: “He who comes from above is above all. He who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all.
units.rightText: He that cometh from above is above all: he that is of the earth is of the earth, and of the earth he speaketh: he that cometh from heaven is above all.

units.leftText: What he has seen and heard, of that he testifies; and no one receives his witness.
units.rightText: What he hath seen and heard, of that he beareth witness; and no man receiveth his witness.

units.leftText: He who has received his witness has set his seal to this, that God is true.
units.rightText: He that hath received his witness hath set his seal to this, that God is true.

units.leftText: For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God; for God gives the Spirit without measure.
units.rightText: For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for he giveth not the Spirit by measure.

units.leftText: The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.
units.rightText: The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.

units.leftText: One who believes in the Son has eternal life, but one who disobeys the Son won’t see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.”
units.rightText: He that believeth on the Son hath eternal life; but he that obeyeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him.
leftNotes: 3:36 The same word can be translated “disobeys” or “disbelieves” in this context.

units.leftText: Therefore when the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John
units.rightText: When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John

units.leftText: (although Jesus himself didn’t baptize, but his disciples),
units.rightText: (although Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples),

units.leftText: he left Judea and departed into Galilee.
units.rightText: he left Judæa, and departed again into Galilee.

units.leftText: He needed to pass through Samaria.
units.rightText: And he must needs pass through Samaria.

units.leftText: So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
units.rightText: So he cometh to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph:

units.leftText: Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
units.rightText: and Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

units.leftText: A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”
units.rightText: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.

units.leftText: For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.
units.rightText: For his disciples were gone away into the city to buy food.

units.leftText: The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
units.rightText: The Samaritan woman therefore saith unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, who am a Samaritan woman? (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)

units.leftText: Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.

units.leftText: They said therefore to him, “What then do you do for a sign, that we may see and believe you? What work do you do?
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, What then doest thou for a sign, that we may see, and believe thee? what workest thou?

units.leftText: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness. As it is written, ‘He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.’”
units.rightText: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written, He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.
leftNotes: 6:31 Greek and Hebrew use the same word for “heaven”, “the heavens”, “the sky”, and “the air”.

units.leftText: Jesus therefore said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, it wasn’t Moses who gave you the bread out of heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread out of heaven.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, It was not Moses that gave you the bread out of heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread out of heaven.

units.leftText: For the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven and gives life to the world.”
units.rightText: For the bread of God is that which cometh down out of heaven, and giveth life unto the world.

units.leftText: They said therefore to him, “Lord, always give us this bread.”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger, and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.

units.leftText: But I told you that you have seen me, and yet you don’t believe.
units.rightText: But I said unto you, that ye have seen me, and yet believe not.

units.leftText: All those whom the Father gives me will come to me. He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.
units.rightText: All that which the Father giveth me shall come unto me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.

units.leftText: For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.
units.rightText: For I am come down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.

units.leftText: This is the will of my Father who sent me, that of all he has given to me I should lose nothing, but should raise him up at the last day.
units.rightText: And this is the will of him that sent me, that of all that which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up at the last day.

units.leftText: This is the will of the one who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.”
units.rightText: For this is the will of my Father, that every one that beholdeth the Son, and believeth on him, should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said, “I am the bread which came down out of heaven.”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said, I am the bread which came down out of heaven.

units.leftText: They said, “Isn’t this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say, ‘I have come down out of heaven’?”
units.rightText: And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how doth he now say, I am come down out of heaven?

units.leftText: Therefore Jesus answered them, “Don’t murmur among yourselves.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.

units.leftText: No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I will raise him up in the last day.
units.rightText: No man can come to me, except the Father that sent me draw him: and I will raise him up in the last day.

units.leftText: It is written in the prophets, ‘They will all be taught by God.’ Therefore everyone who hears from the Father and has learned, comes to me.
units.rightText: It is written in the prophets, And they shall all be taught of God. Every one that hath heard from the Father, and hath learned, cometh unto me.

units.leftText: Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God. He has seen the Father.
units.rightText: Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he that is from God, he hath seen the Father.

units.leftText: Most certainly, I tell you, he who believes in me has eternal life.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth hath eternal life.

units.leftText: I am the bread of life.
units.rightText: I am the bread of life.

units.leftText: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and they died.
units.rightText: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.

units.leftText: This is the bread which comes down out of heaven, that anyone may eat of it and not die.
units.rightText: This is the bread which cometh down out of heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.

units.leftText: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”
units.rightText: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: yea and the bread which I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore contended with one another, saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore strove one with another, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?

units.leftText: Jesus therefore said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you don’t have life in yourselves.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, ye have not life in yourselves.

units.leftText: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
units.rightText: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

units.leftText: For my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.
units.rightText: For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.

units.leftText: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood lives in me, and I in him.
units.rightText: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me, and I in him.

units.leftText: As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so he who feeds on me will also live because of me.
units.rightText: As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father; so he that eateth me, he also shall live because of me.

units.leftText: This is the bread which came down out of heaven—not as our fathers ate the manna and died. He who eats this bread will live forever.”
units.rightText: This is the bread which came down out of heaven: not as the fathers ate, and died; he that eateth this bread shall live for ever.

units.leftText: He said these things in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.
units.rightText: These things said he in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.

units.leftText: Therefore many of his disciples, when they heard this, said, “This is a hard saying! Who can listen to it?”
units.rightText: Many therefore of his disciples, when they heard this, said, This is a hard saying; who can hear it?

units.leftText: But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said to them, “Does this cause you to stumble?
units.rightText: But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said unto them, Doth this cause you to stumble?

units.leftText: Then what if you would see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?
units.rightText: What then if ye should behold the Son of man ascending where he was before?

units.leftText: It is the spirit who gives life. The flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and are life.
units.rightText: It is the spirit that giveth life; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I have spoken unto you are spirit, and are life.

units.leftText: But there are some of you who don’t believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who didn’t believe, and who it was who would betray him.
units.rightText: But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who it was that should betray him.

units.leftText: He said, “For this cause I have said to you that no one can come to me, unless it is given to him by my Father.”
units.rightText: And he said, For this cause have I said unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it be given unto him of the Father.

units.leftText: At this, many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him.
units.rightText: Upon this many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.

units.leftText: Jesus said therefore to the twelve, “You don’t also want to go away, do you?”
units.rightText: Jesus said therefore unto the twelve, Would ye also go away?

units.leftText: Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
units.rightText: Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

units.leftText: We have come to believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
units.rightText: And we have believed and know that thou art the Holy One of God.

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Didn’t I choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?”
units.rightText: Jesus answered them, Did not I choose you the twelve, and one of you is a devil?

units.leftText: Now he spoke of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for it was he who would betray him, being one of the twelve.
units.rightText: Now he spake of Judas the son of Simon Iscariot, for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve.

units.leftText: After these things, Jesus was walking in Galilee, for he wouldn’t walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him.
units.rightText: And after these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Judæa, because the Jews sought to kill him.

units.leftText: Now the feast of the Jews, the Feast of Booths, was at hand.
units.rightText: Now the feast of the Jews, the feast of tabernacles, was at hand.

units.leftText: His brothers therefore said to him, “Depart from here and go into Judea, that your disciples also may see your works which you do.
units.rightText: His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judæa, that thy disciples also may behold thy works which thou doest.

units.leftText: For no one does anything in secret while he seeks to be known openly. If you do these things, reveal yourself to the world.”
units.rightText: For no man doeth anything in secret, and himself seeketh to be known openly. If thou doest these things, manifest thyself to the world.

units.leftText: For even his brothers didn’t believe in him.
units.rightText: For even his brethren did not believe on him.

units.leftText: Jesus therefore said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore saith unto them, My time is not yet come; but your time is always ready.

units.leftText: The world can’t hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it, that its works are evil.
units.rightText: The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that its works are evil.

units.leftText: You go up to the feast. I am not yet going up to this feast, because my time is not yet fulfilled.”
units.rightText: Go ye up unto the feast: I go not up unto this feast; because my time is not yet fulfilled.

units.leftText: Having said these things to them, he stayed in Galilee.
units.rightText: And having said these things unto them, he abode still in Galilee.

units.leftText: But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not publicly, but as it were in secret.
units.rightText: But when his brethren were gone up unto the feast, then went he also up, not publicly, but as it were in secret.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, “Where is he?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he?

units.leftText: There was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him. Some said, “He is a good man.” Others said, “Not so, but he leads the multitude astray.”
units.rightText: And there was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him: some said, He is a good man; others said, Not so, but he leadeth the multitude astray.

units.leftText: Yet no one spoke openly of him for fear of the Jews.
units.rightText: Yet no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews.

units.leftText: But when it was now the middle of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple and taught.
units.rightText: But when it was now the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore marveled, saying, “How does this man know letters, having never been educated?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?

units.leftText: Jesus therefore answered them, “My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore answered them, and said, My teaching is not mine, but his that sent me.

units.leftText: If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or if I am speaking from myself.
units.rightText: If any man willeth to do his will, he shall know of the teaching, whether it is of God, or whether I speak from myself.

units.leftText: He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory, but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.
units.rightText: He that speaketh from himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh the glory of him that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.

units.leftText: Didn’t Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill me?”
units.rightText: Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you doeth the law? Why seek ye to kill me?

units.leftText: The multitude answered, “You have a demon! Who seeks to kill you?”
units.rightText: The multitude answered, Thou hast a demon: who seeketh to kill thee?

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “I did one work and you all marvel because of it.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, I did one work, and ye all marvel because thereof.

units.leftText: Moses has given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers), and on the Sabbath you circumcise a boy.
units.rightText: Moses hath given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers); and on the sabbath ye circumcise a man.

units.leftText: If a boy receives circumcision on the Sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a man completely healthy on the Sabbath?
units.rightText: If a man receiveth circumcision on the sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken; are ye wroth with me, because I made a man every whit whole on the sabbath?

units.leftText: Don’t judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.”
units.rightText: Judge not according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.

units.leftText: Therefore some of them of Jerusalem said, “Isn’t this he whom they seek to kill?
units.rightText: Some therefore of them of Jerusalem said, Is not this he whom they seek to kill?

units.leftText: Behold, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is truly the Christ?
units.rightText: And lo, he speaketh openly, and they say nothing unto him. Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is the Christ?

units.leftText: However, we know where this man comes from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.”
units.rightText: Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when the Christ cometh, no one knoweth whence he is.

units.leftText: Jesus therefore cried out in the temple, teaching and saying, “You both know me, and know where I am from. I have not come of myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you don’t know.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore cried in the temple, teaching and saying, Ye both know me, and know whence I am; and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not.

units.leftText: I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”
units.rightText: I know him; because I am from him, and he sent me.

units.leftText: They sought therefore to take him; but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.
units.rightText: They sought therefore to take him: and no man laid his hand on him, because his hour was not yet come.

units.leftText: But of the multitude, many believed in him. They said, “When the Christ comes, he won’t do more signs than those which this man has done, will he?”
units.rightText: But of the multitude many believed on him; and they said, When the Christ shall come, will he do more signs than those which this man hath done?

units.leftText: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him.
units.rightText: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him; and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to take him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said, “I will be with you a little while longer, then I go to him who sent me.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said, Yet a little while am I with you, and I go unto him that sent me.

units.leftText: You will seek me and won’t find me. You can’t come where I am.”
units.rightText: Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, ye cannot come.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore said among themselves, “Where will this man go that we won’t find him? Will he go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said among themselves, Whither will this man go that we shall not find him? will he go unto the Dispersion among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?

units.leftText: What is this word that he said, ‘You will seek me, and won’t find me;’ and ‘Where I am, you can’t come’?”
units.rightText: What is this word that he said, Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me; and where I am, ye cannot come?

units.leftText: Now on the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!
units.rightText: Now on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

units.leftText: He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water.”
units.rightText: He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, from within him shall flow rivers of living water.

units.leftText: But he said this about the Spirit, which those believing in him were to receive. For the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus wasn’t yet glorified.
units.rightText: But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believed on him were to receive: for the Spirit was not yet given; because Jesus was not yet glorified.

units.leftText: Many of the multitude therefore, when they heard these words, said, “This is truly the prophet.”
units.rightText: Some of the multitude therefore, when they heard these words, said, This is of a truth the prophet.

units.leftText: Others said, “This is the Christ.” But some said, “What, does the Christ come out of Galilee?
units.rightText: Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, What, doth the Christ come out of Galilee?

units.leftText: Hasn’t the Scripture said that the Christ comes of the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”
units.rightText: Hath not the scripture said that the Christ cometh of the seed of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?

units.leftText: So a division arose in the multitude because of him.
units.rightText: So there arose a division in the multitude because of him.

units.leftText: Some of them would have arrested him, but no one laid hands on him.
units.rightText: And some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him.

units.leftText: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said to them, “Why didn’t you bring him?”
units.rightText: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why did ye not bring him?

units.leftText: The officers answered, “No man ever spoke like this man!”
units.rightText: The officers answered, Never man so spake.

units.leftText: The Pharisees therefore answered them, “You aren’t also led astray, are you?
units.rightText: The Pharisees therefore answered them, Are ye also led astray?

units.leftText: Have any of the rulers or any of the Pharisees believed in him?
units.rightText: Hath any of the rulers believed on him, or of the Pharisees?

units.leftText: But this multitude that doesn’t know the law is cursed.”
units.rightText: But this multitude that knoweth not the law are accursed.

units.leftText: Nicodemus (he who came to him by night, being one of them) said to them,
units.rightText: Nicodemus saith unto them (he that came to him before, being one of them),

units.leftText: “Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him personally and knows what he does?”
units.rightText: Doth our law judge a man, except it first hear from himself and know what he doeth?

units.leftText: They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see that no prophet has arisen out of Galilee.”
units.rightText: They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and see that out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.

units.leftText: Everyone went to his own house,
units.rightText: [And they went every man unto his own house:

units.leftText: but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
units.rightText: but Jesus went unto the mount of Olives.

units.leftText: Now very early in the morning, he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him. He sat down and taught them.
units.rightText: And early in the morning he came again into the temple, and all the people came unto him; and he sat down, and taught them.

units.leftText: The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle,
units.rightText: And the scribes and the Pharisees bring a woman taken in adultery; and having set her in the midst,

units.leftText: they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act.
units.rightText: they say unto him, Teacher, this woman hath been taken in adultery, in the very act.

units.leftText: Now in our law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say about her?”
units.rightText: Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such: what then sayest thou of her?

units.leftText: They said this testing him, that they might have something to accuse him of.
units.rightText: And this they said, trying him, that they might have whereof to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground.

units.leftText: But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.”
units.rightText: But when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.

units.leftText: Again he stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
units.rightText: And again he stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground.

units.leftText: They, when they heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the oldest, even to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman where she was, in the middle.
units.rightText: And they, when they heard it, went out one by one, beginning from the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman, where she was, in the midst.

units.leftText: Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?”
units.rightText: And Jesus lifted up himself, and said unto her, Woman, where are they? did no man condemn thee?

units.leftText: She said, “No one, Lord.”
units.rightText: And she said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said, Neither do I condemn thee: go thy way; from henceforth sin no more.]

units.leftText: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
units.rightText: Again therefore Jesus spake unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in the darkness, but shall have the light of life.

units.leftText: The Pharisees therefore said to him, “You testify about yourself. Your testimony is not valid.”
units.rightText: The Pharisees therefore said unto him, Thou bearest witness of thyself; thy witness is not true.

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, for I know where I came from, and where I am going; but you don’t know where I came from, or where I am going.
units.rightText: Jesus answered and said unto them, Even if I bear witness of myself, my witness is true; for I know whence I came, and whither I go; but ye know not whence I come, or whither I go.

units.leftText: You judge according to the flesh. I judge no one.
units.rightText: Ye judge after the flesh; I judge no man.

units.leftText: Even if I do judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone, but I am with the Father who sent me.
units.rightText: Yea and if I judge, my judgment is true; for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me.

units.leftText: It’s also written in your law that the testimony of two people is valid.
units.rightText: Yea and in your law it is written, that the witness of two men is true.

units.leftText: I am one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”
units.rightText: I am he that beareth witness of myself, and the Father that sent me beareth witness of me.

units.leftText: They said therefore to him, “Where is your Father?”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Where is thy Father? Jesus answered, Ye know neither me, nor my Father: if ye knew me, ye would know my Father also.

units.leftText: Jesus spoke these words in the treasury, as he taught in the temple. Yet no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.
units.rightText: These words spake he in the treasury, as he taught in the temple: and no man took him; because his hour was not yet come.

units.leftText: Jesus said therefore again to them, “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sins. Where I go, you can’t come.”
units.rightText: He said therefore again unto them, I go away, and ye shall seek me, and shall die in your sin: whither I go, ye cannot come.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore said, “Will he kill himself, because he says, ‘Where I am going, you can’t come’?”
units.rightText: The Jews therefore said, Will he kill himself, that he saith, Whither I go, ye cannot come?

units.leftText: He said to them, “You are from beneath. I am from above. You are of this world. I am not of this world.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world.

units.leftText: I said therefore to you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”
units.rightText: I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: for except ye believe that I am he, ye shall die in your sins.

units.leftText: They said therefore to him, “Who are you?”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, Who art thou? Jesus said unto them, Even that which I have also spoken unto you from the beginning.

units.leftText: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you. However, he who sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these I say to the world.”
units.rightText: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you: howbeit he that sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these speak I unto the world.

units.leftText: They didn’t understand that he spoke to them about the Father.
units.rightText: They perceived not that he spake to them of the Father.

units.leftText: Jesus therefore said to them, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and I do nothing of myself, but as my Father taught me, I say these things.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said, When ye have lifted up the Son of man, then shall ye know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father taught me, I speak these things.

units.leftText: He who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone, for I always do the things that are pleasing to him.”
units.rightText: And he that sent me is with me; he hath not left me alone; for I do always the things that are pleasing to him.

units.leftText: As he spoke these things, many believed in him.
units.rightText: As he spake these things, many believed on him.

units.leftText: Jesus therefore said to those Jews who had believed him, “If you remain in my word, then you are truly my disciples.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said to those Jews that had believed him, If ye abide in my word, then are ye truly my disciples;

units.leftText: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
units.rightText: and ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

units.leftText: They answered him, “We are Abraham’s offspring, and have never been in bondage to anyone. How do you say, ‘You will be made free’?”

units.leftText: But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do this.

units.leftText: Therefore Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would love me, for I came out and have come from God. For I haven’t come of myself, but he sent me.
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, If God were your Father, ye would love me: for I came forth and am come from God; for neither have I come of myself, but he sent me.

units.leftText: Why don’t you understand my speech? Because you can’t hear my word.
units.rightText: Why do ye not understand my speech? Even because ye cannot hear my word.

units.leftText: You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks on his own; for he is a liar, and the father of lies.
units.rightText: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father it is your will to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and standeth not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father thereof.

units.leftText: But because I tell the truth, you don’t believe me.

units.leftText: Then the Jews answered him, “Don’t we say well that you are a Samaritan, and have a demon?”

units.leftText: But I don’t seek my own glory. There is one who seeks and judges.

units.rightText: The Jews said unto him, Now we know that thou hast a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets; and thou sayest, If a man keep my word, he shall never taste of death.

units.leftText: Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died. Who do you make yourself out to be?”

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is our God.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing: it is my Father that glorifieth me; of whom ye say, that he is your God;

units.leftText: You have not known him, but I know him. If I said, ‘I don’t know him,’ I would be like you, a liar. But I know him and keep his word.

units.leftText: The Jews therefore said to him, “You are not yet fifty years old! Have you seen Abraham?”

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, before Abraham came into existence, I AM. ”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was born, I am.

units.leftText: His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “This man didn’t sin, nor did his parents, but that the works of God might be revealed in him.

units.leftText: I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day. The night is coming, when no one can work.

units.rightText: and said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam (which is by interpretation, Sent). He went away therefore, and washed, and came seeing.

units.rightText: and asked them, saying, Is this your son, who ye say was born blind? how then doth he now see?

units.rightText: Therefore said his parents, He is of age; ask him.

units.rightText: So they called a second time the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give glory to God: we know that this man is a sinner.

units.leftText: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
units.rightText: He therefore answered, Whether he is a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.

units.leftText: They said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
units.rightText: They said therefore unto him, What did he to thee? how opened he thine eyes?

units.leftText: He answered them, “I told you already, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You don’t also want to become his disciples, do you?”
units.rightText: He answered them, I told you even now, and ye did not hear; wherefore would ye hear it again? would ye also become his disciples?

units.leftText: They insulted him and said, “You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
units.rightText: And they reviled him, and said, Thou art his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses.

units.leftText: We know that God has spoken to Moses. But as for this man, we don’t know where he comes from.”
units.rightText: We know that God hath spoken unto Moses: but as for this man, we know not whence he is.

units.leftText: The man answered them, “How amazing! You don’t know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.
units.rightText: The man answered and said unto them, Why, herein is the marvel, that ye know not whence he is, and yet he opened mine eyes.

units.leftText: We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners, but if anyone is a worshiper of God and does his will, he listens to him.
units.rightText: We know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and do his will, him he heareth.

units.leftText: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”

units.leftText: They answered him, “You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us?” Then they threw him out.
units.rightText: They answered and said unto him, Thou wast altogether born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they cast him out.

units.leftText: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”
units.rightText: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and finding him, he said, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?

units.leftText: He answered, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”
units.rightText: He answered and said, And who is he, Lord, that I may believe on him?

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”
units.rightText: Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and he it is that speaketh with thee.

units.leftText: He said, “Lord, I believe!” and he worshiped him.
units.rightText: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.

units.leftText: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, that those who don’t see may see; and that those who see may become blind.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said, For judgment came I into this world, that they that see not may see; and that they that see may become blind.

units.leftText: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said to him, “Are we also blind?”
units.rightText: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said unto him, Are we also blind?

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye would have no sin: but now ye say, We see: your sin remaineth.

units.leftText: “Most certainly, I tell you, one who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheep fold, but climbs up some other way, is a thief and a robber.
units.rightText: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.

units.leftText: But one who enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
units.rightText: But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.

units.leftText: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
units.rightText: To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.

units.leftText: Whenever he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice.
units.rightText: When he hath put forth all his own, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice.

units.leftText: They will by no means follow a stranger, but will flee from him; for they don’t know the voice of strangers.”
units.rightText: And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.

units.leftText: Jesus spoke this parable to them, but they didn’t understand what he was telling them.
units.rightText: This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things they were which he spake unto them.

units.leftText: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Most certainly, I tell you, I am the sheep’s door.
units.rightText: Jesus therefore said unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.

units.leftText: I am the door. If anyone enters in by me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and will find pasture.
units.rightText: I am the door; by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and go out, and shall find pasture.

units.leftText: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
units.rightText: The thief cometh not, but that he may steal, and kill, and destroy: I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.

units.leftText: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
units.rightText: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd layeth down his life for the sheep.

units.leftText: I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I’m known by my own;

units.rightText: even as the Father knoweth me, and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.

units.rightText: And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and they shall become one flock, one shepherd.

units.leftText: Therefore the Father loves me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again.
units.rightText: Therefore doth the Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again.

units.rightText: No one taketh it away from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment received I from my Father.

units.rightText: The Jews answered him, For a good work we stone thee not, but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.
